subject: MSA / Order Form redlines — OSS pass-through and caps / consequential damages
messages:

Subject: Redlines to MSA + Order Form (liability / OSS pass-through)

Hi Lauren / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are the redlines our legal and procurement teams proposed for the MSA and the Order Form (OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf). High-level items we want to call out so you have context before reviewing:

- Liability cap: we need the Order Form to carve out claims relating to third-party open-source model licensing and IP. Our procurement policy requires pass-through indemnity for OSS that causes IP exposure.
- Consequential damages: we want consequential damages excluded except where caused by willful misconduct or gross negligence.
- OSS indemnity: in cases where a model vendor or OSS supplier is upstream, ByteWorks needs Redwood to accept pass-through obligations to the same extent Redwood is protected by its suppliers.

We recognize some of this is non-standard — happy to discuss tradeoffs. Can we schedule a 30m call with your contracts team tomorrow?

Best,
Samir

Samir — thanks for sending and for the clear summary. I’ve looped in Marcus (legal) and Priyom (contracts) so we can get a legal read and propose language quickly.

Initial asks from our side:
- We can live with limited pass-through in narrow circumstances, but we cannot agree to uncapped pass-through or broad upstream obligations that exceed our own suppliers’ liability.
- For OSS/model licensing we typically require: (a) representation that licensed OSS does not infringe third-party IP, (b) acceptance of indemnity only where the OSS is provided under vendor-controlled licensing terms and the vendor has primary responsibility to defend/indemnify, and (c) a specified monetary cap for pass-through tied to the supplier's upstream cap.
- Consequential damages: Redwood’s standard is to exclude consequential/indirect damages broadly; carve-outs for gross negligence/fraud are acceptable.

Marcus / Priyom — can you review the attached redlines and propose concrete redline language (short snippet) we can send back to ByteWorks today? Also flag anything that would materially increase Redwood’s exposure so I can loop in VP ops if needed.

Happy to do a 30m sync this afternoon.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-04-12T13:27:00Z
Subject: Re: Redlines to MSA + Order Form (liability / OSS pass-through)

Thanks for the heads up, Lauren. I reviewed the PDF and outlined our recommended position below — high level then proposed redline snippets. Attachment: legal_note_oss_pass_through.txt (notes + text snippets).

High-level position:
- Pass-through indemnity: accept only where Redwood is contractually required to provide indemnity to the customer as a direct result of an upstream supplier's breach of its own warranty/indemnity obligations and only to the extent Redwood actually recovers the same from that supplier. In short: "pass-through where there is recovery against the upstream supplier". We should refuse open-ended passthrough that creates a de facto unlimited liability.
- OSS/model licensing: require vendor to represent that OSS included is properly licensed and to provide the upstream supplier contact and license terms. If claim arises from upstream OSS, Redwood's obligation should be limited to the lesser of (a) Redwood's liability cap and (b) any recovery Redwood obtains from the upstream supplier.
- Caps and consequential damages: keep the global liability cap in the MSA (e.g., greater of fees paid over past 12 months or $X) and retain consequential damages exclusion except for (i) gross negligence/willful misconduct and (ii) IP infringement claims where statutory remedies may apply.

Proposed redline snippet (suggested language to send to ByteWorks):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, Supplier (Redwood) shall have no liability for indirect, consequential or special damages, except to the extent such damages result from Supplier's gross negligence or willful misconduct. For claims relating to third-party open source software (including model weights, adapters, or other components licensed from third parties), Supplier's indemnity obligations shall be limited to damages Recoverable from the applicable upstream supplier, and in no event shall Supplier's aggregate liability exceed the Liability Cap set forth in the Order Form."

Operational considerations: require notice and opportunity to remediate; require ByteWorks to pursue upstream supplier first; preserve Redwood's right to join upstream vendor in defense.

If ByteWorks insists on a separate carve-out that removes the cap for OSS-related IP claims, recommend we escalate to VP Legal and offer an alternative commercial solution (e.g., increased cap for that order or procurement of an IP insurance rider).

I’ll prepare tracked-changes and send to Lauren/Karthik in 60–90 mins.

Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, Samir Patel <samir.patel@byteworks.com>
Date: 2026-04-13T11:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Redlines to MSA + Order Form (liability / OSS pass-through)

Looping in commercial context — appreciate the legal analysis Marcus. From the customer side, they are pushing hard on an OSS carve-out tied to their procurement policy. If we push back too hard, risk losing the deal or getting delayed procurement approval.

Proposed approach: send ByteWorks Marcus's redline with 2 options:
1) Redwood standard — pass-through limited to recoveries from upstream supplier plus cap retained.
2) For expedited approval, a transitional concession: for the first 12 months only, Redwood will accept a pass-through limited to direct damages up to $250k, subject to Redwood's right to seek recovery from upstream suppliers, and contingent on ByteWorks providing upstream supplier contact details and a covenant to pursue upstream remedies.

If ByteWorks accepts option 2, we treat as a commercial concession tied to the current order and subject to an amended cap for renewal. Thoughts?

Karthik
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Commercially, ByteWorks would prefer a permanent carve-out but we can consider the transitional concession you proposed for an initial deployment while we validate model supplier terms.

Next steps:
- Procurement will share the supplier contacts and license records for the models referenced in our use case by Friday.
- Let's set a 30m call Monday 4/20 to finalize the specific Order Form wording — procurement + legal on our side, and Laurel / Marcus on yours. (If Monday doesn't work we'll propose alternatives.)

Appreciate the flexibility.

Best,
Samir
